Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: Chest tightness for ~3 hours with wheeze and cough; mild shortness of breath. Recent cold symptoms (last week) with sore throat and runny nose; feeling under the weather.
- Onset, duration, progression: Symptoms started ~3 hours ago; persistent; cough non-productive; cough worse at night; SOB with exertion but not at rest.
- Past medical history: Asthma (since adolescence) with prior severe exacerbation requiring intubation during high school; eczema in childhood; milk protein allergy; hay fever; dust allergy.
- Medications: Inhalers previously used but not currently available:
  - Ventolin (salbutamol) inhaler
  - Clenil Modulite inhaler
  - Both ran out about a week ago; not used in the past week
- Allergies: Drug allergies denied; environmental/dust allergy noted.
- Social history: Not documented.

- Investigations/results: None provided.

Assessment & Plan:
1) Acute asthma exacerbation with viral URI features
   - Assessment: Likely asthma flare triggered by recent viral upper respiratory infection; symptoms include wheeze, non-productive cough, exertional dyspnea, chest tightness.
   - Differential diagnoses: Viral bronchitis; pneumonia (less likely given history; no focal findings documented).
   - Investigations planned: None documented.
   - Treatment planned:
     - Prescriptions for inhalers to be provided: Salbutamol (Ventolin) inhaler PRN; Clenil Modulite inhaler (controller) to be used in the morning with Ventolin PRN.
     - Oral corticosteroids: five-day course; two tablets each morning (drug name not specified; dose/frequency documented).
     - Spacer device to improve inhaled deposition; instructions to be provided.
     - Education on steroid side effects; read label; steroids generally well tolerated.
     - Activity/work: self-certify for 7 days; rest as needed until improved.
     - Safety follow-up: seek medical attention if Ventolin use exceeds every 3 hours or if deterioration (worsening SOB, chest pain, dizziness).
   - Referrals: Not indicated.
